adjudicated.jp: 誰もいない。
adjudicated.en: There is no one.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ここ数日、冬子を見ていない気がする。
adjudicated.en: It feels like I haven't seen Touko at all these last few days.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「気にくわないこともあるだろうけど、明日から部活、来てみないか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I know you can't really stomach it, but couldn't you try coming to Club starting tomorrow?"
adjudicated.assessment: The generic noun requires an article and should not be capitalized as an unexplained proper name.

adjudicated.jp: などと独白する。
adjudicated.en: And that's how my soliloquy goes.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 冬子がいたら、そう言ってやろうと思っていたのだ。
adjudicated.en: If Youko had been among us, that's what I thought I would be telling her.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says what he intended to tell Touko. The English substitutes Youko, changing the referenced person in the reflection.

highlights.text: If Youko had been among us

adjudicated.jp: 青春ごっこをするなら、全員がいい。
adjudicated.en: If we're going to play Pretend-an-Adolescence, it'd be best with all hands.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 今日は日記も記し甲斐がある。
adjudicated.en: It's worthwhile to diarize in the diary today, too.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ちなみに『日記を記す』は文法上の間違いじゃないぞ。
adjudicated.en: By the way, "diarize in the diary" ain't grammatically incorrect ya know.
comments: Song reference. Well, it's "to jot down in a diary in a diary", but redundancy's more of a grammar misdemeanor anyway. That's what they told me at the local PD Department when they released me on bail, at least. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 日記は名詞だからな。
adjudicated.en: Diary is a noun after all.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: などと額になるようなことも織り交ぜつつ、カキカキしていく。
adjudicated.en: Interwoven with this and several other things that become picture frames, I continue with the scribbling.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ※額になる＝太一誤字。学になる、が正しい。太一は『知識は額縁のように自分を彩ってくれる』というような意味合いで間違えている。
adjudicated.en:
* Become picture frames (sic). Correct is 'become
erudition'. Taichi misunderstood the exact
implication of "knowledge decorates the self like
a frame decorates a picture".
comments: To the surprise of at this point no one, I can't actually source that as a real proverb. I'd wonder why, exactly, he's jotting down these silly and pointless notes in something no one will likely ever read, but somehow after writing that the fabric of the universe seems to have grown slightly weaker... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: できたら日曜日には全員集合といきたいものだ。
adjudicated.en: If possible, I would like to gather all hands on Sunday.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: あー、日曜は日記に記録できないな。
adjudicated.en: Ahhh, Sunday I can't diarize any record in the diary, no.
comments: Sure, 日記に記録 is different, but there's no way he doesn't mean this. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: でも、そういう光景を一度見ておきたい。
adjudicated.en: Still, that's one scene I would like to see at least once.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: リセットは、もしかするとすごく恐い現象だ。
adjudicated.en: The reset might just be a very frightening phenomenon,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 死と同一の。
adjudicated.en: identical to death.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: だから……せめて……。
adjudicated.en: That's why... at the very least...
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「誘ってみるか……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Should I try inviting them..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 郵便局に向かう。
adjudicated.en: I head to the post office.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 強襲、郵便局。
adjudicated.en: I go postal.
comments: I assert that this is a literal translation. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 強襲、郵便局 jokingly frames the post office visit as a raid or assault. The English imports an unrelated idiom for workplace violence.

adjudicated.jp: ハガキを三十枚ほど強奪する。
adjudicated.en: I plunder around thirty postcards.
comments: Hum, all I got is that postcard paper for inkjet printers is sold in packs of 30... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 帰りは、これみよがしに交番の前を通ってくる。
adjudicated.en: On the way back, I ostentatiously pass back and forth in front of the kouban.
comments: Bored policeman 1: "Oh, it's one of those weirdos." -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

adjudicated.jp: ついでに交番も強襲しておく。
adjudicated.en: While I'm there, I also assault the kouban.
comments: Bored policeman 2: "If he's not doing anything, just leave him do his thing, less trouble." (Console version censors this, but saying "I'll intrude on the kouban" is even more explicit!) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

adjudicated.jp: 入るのははじめてだった。
adjudicated.en: It was the first time I'd been inside one.
comments: See CCA0021. Notice a sign of something missing? And yet it should've been there since Monday unchanged. Clever clever. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ほー、これが交番の内部かー」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, so thiiis is what the inside of a Kouban looks like."
comments: Bored policeman 1: "Yes indeed, yes indeed. Yeah, he's harmless." -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked and unnecessarily capitalized Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

adjudicated.jp: 拳銃とかないのかな。
adjudicated.en: Are there handguns here I wonder.
comments: Bored policeman 2: "They're in a safe of course." -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 手錠があった。
adjudicated.en: There were handcuffs.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 他にめぼしいものはない。
adjudicated.en: There were no other valuables.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「いけね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Cut it out now."
comments: Bored policeman 2: "Good evening to you too, I guess." Bored policeman 1: "...all kinds around here, all kinds..." -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: いけね is Taichi's realization, 'Oops' or 'Oh, right.' The English turns it into a command directed at someone else.

adjudicated.jp: こんなことしてる時間はない。
adjudicated.en: I don't have time to do this kind of stuff.
comments: It's just rubbed into people's faces, really. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 急いで帰る。
adjudicated.en: I hurry back home.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ハガキを書く。
adjudicated.en: I write the postcards.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「さてと……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And then now..."
adjudicated.assessment: さてと is a transition such as 'Well, then.' The English phrase is not idiomatic.

adjudicated.jp: 方々に。
adjudicated.en: This way, and that way.
adjudicated.assessment: 方々に means he writes to various people or destinations. The English substitutes vague directions and loses the postcard recipients.

adjudicated.jp: 慌ただしい夜である。
adjudicated.en: A busy night we will have here.
comments: He just dumps 'em in the post, doesn't he. And it's like 5PM anyway. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator states that it is a hectic night. The English changes this to an awkward future forecast.

highlights.text: A busy night we will have here
